description: #195, fixed decision 2: `"integration_baseline": []` is a DECLARATION — "this repository has no integration verification" — and it is never answered with `baseline`. The profile here declares a perfectly runnable `baseline` (`cat cmate-verify-ok`, green in the merged checkout), so a runner whose fallback keyed off the list being EMPTY rather than the key being ABSENT would merge both PRs and report a green integration verification. This case is the opposite: refused before the first merge (failure / preflight_failed / integration_verify_unavailable, exit 1), `git fetch` never called, nothing merged, and `source: integration_baseline` with `commands: []` recording which declaration was read. The next action is the one the operator can act on — write the definition of green, or remove the key — and NOT m25's "declare a baseline", which would be advice to undo the declaration they made on purpose.
